svg.title: What one change costs a script view, on three paths
svg.desc: Three lanes, their bars drawn to the same scale. First: nothing the view reads changed, so no script runs at all and the frame replays the description already published — no bar. Second, what happens today when a value changes: the whole panel is described again at 0.315 milliseconds, however small the change, drawn as a long orange bar. Third, the same change with the row a retained view of its own: 0.012 milliseconds, a bar about a twenty-sixth as long, because nine nodes are described instead of 361. The snapshot cache removes the first lane's cost and does nothing for the second; only a smaller invalidation boundary does.
svg.text: What one change costs, and where the snapshot cache stops
Bars to scale. Measured on a 40-row watchlist, release build, best of seven batches of fifty.
the frame replays the description already published
A value changed — what happens today
the whole panel is described again, however small the change
The same change, with the row a view of its own
9 nodes described instead of 361 — the lever this page opens with
The snapshot cache removes the first lane. It does nothing for the second — only a smaller boundary does.
